summary:
# NOTES ON TWO BOOKS (Evelyn Raymond, Dorothy series, Platt & Peck / Hurst; Gutenberg ids 41117 and 40300)

## BOOK 1: "DOROTHY AT SKYRIE" (1907, Platt & Peck, illustrated; frontispiece "HOW MUCH AM I BID FOR THE BEAUTIFUL CALICO PONY?")

Chapter list: I Early Visitors; II An Unfortunate Affair; III On the Road to South Meadow; IV The Learned Blacksmith; V An Accident and an Apparition; VI More Peculiar Visitors; VII At the Office of a Justice; VIII A Walk and Its Ending; IX A Live Stock Sale; X At Milking-Time; XI Helpers; XII Seth Winters and His Friends; XIII A Beneficent Bee; XIV An Astonishing Question; XV Concerning Several Matters; XVI The Fate of Daisy-Jewel; XVII On the Road to the Circus; XVIII That South Meadow; XIX Dorothy Has Another Secret; XX All's Well That Ends Well.

**Setting:** Skyrie, a stone-walled hill farm "up-mounting" in the Highlands of the Hudson near Riverside (Upper and Lower Riverside villages), near Newburgh. Dorothy's new home. Neighbors: Deerhurst (Mrs. Calvert's mansion, lodge, gate, Great Danes), the Towers (Montaigne house), Heartsease (Oliver Sands's farm), Cat Hollow (Babcock home), Judge Satterlee's place, Mis' Calvert's woods, Si Waterman's south meadow ("Si Waterman's Folly", a shaft/mine), Ghost-legend of Skyrie. Baltimore home was 77 Brown Street.

**Characters:**
- Dorothy Chester (Dorothy C.), foundling/adopted girl, ~12, birthday April 2; parents John Chester ("Dad", "Johnnie", ex-postman, crippled) and Martha ("mother Martha", frugal, prone to fret).
- Mrs. Betty Cecil Somerset-Calvert (Mrs. Cecil, Mrs. Calvert, "Cousin Betty"), wealthy, old, aristocratic Maryland widow of Deerhurst; Great Danes Peter and Ponce; coachman Ephraim (half-deaf, dialect), maid Dinah.
- Jim Barlow, orphan farm boy, rescued Dorothy from Miranda Stott's truck farm; works at Deerhurst; wants education; calls Mrs. Calvert "Mis' Calvert."
- Seth Winters, "Learned Blacksmith," justice of the peace, smithy near Deerhurst, "Great Balm of Gilead" tree; Mrs. Calvert's "Cousin."
- Alfaretta (Alfy), Baretta (Retty), Claretta (Clary), Diaretta (Diary/baby) Babcock; mother (Mis' Babcock, licks Saturdays); father "Pa Babcock," self-styled "Nanarchist," red hair, bragging orator, hired man for a while.
- Archibald Montaigne (rich, pompous, snob, mill/market speculator), wife Mrs. Montaigne (timid), daughter Helena (14, frail, haughty, later kind), son Herbert (handsome, rowdy, horse "Bucephalus", catboat "Merry Chanter", kind to Dorothy; saves Jim's life later). Governess Miss Milliken.
- Oliver Sands, Quaker miller, mortgage holder, "Friend Oliver," sells cow Hannah and calf for $50; holds $300 note "payable on demand"; wants south meadow.
- Peter Piper, half-witted man in red-feathered cap and oilcloth coat; later calls himself "Ghost" who secretly tilled garden, saves Dorothy in the mine.
- Mr. Smith (surveyor/lawyer type not in this book), Bill Barry (auctioneer, horse trader), Mr. Spence (postmaster, Lower Riverside), Mr. Montaigne vs Jim scuffle; Ephraim's dialect.
- Mr. Chester's sister? (none). Mrs. Smith (neighbor, dialect), John Smith (neighbor, boss of "bee"), Mrs. Stott / Miranda Stott (truck-farmer, Jim's former employer), Kidder & Kidder (Mrs. Cecil's lawyers, Baltimore Street), Mrs. Turnbull, Sarah Spencer (pies).

**Events in order:**
1. Alfaretta Babcock and sisters meet Dorothy at the stone wall while she picks wild strawberries; they take her pail; Alfaretta tells of Skyrie's history and Dorothy's kidnapping; Alfy says Ma licks Saturdays; Dorothy hears of gold mine and ghost. Alfy brings berries to Mrs. Chester.
2. Jim arrives with Great Danes Peter and Ponce and a basket from Mrs. Calvert; dogs break loose, run to Lower Riverside. Jim is introduced to Babcocks. Jim refuses breakfast, gives letter to Mr. Chester (signed Elisabeth Cecil Somerset-Calvert, "Important. Not to be opened until after my death"). Mrs. Chester hides letter.
3. Dogs chase; in Lower Riverside post-office Jim knocks down Mr. Montaigne; Jim strikes him; Montaigne demands justice; Mr. Spence sends them to Seth Winters, justice up-mountain. Winters takes Jim under wing ("Come with me, my lad").
4. Ephraim finds dogs at kennel with broken chains; Mrs. Calvert's "My Miss Betty" pistol talk.
5. Winters walks with Jim, talks of caterpillar spared, invites confession; Jim begs for job, refused. At Deerhurst Jim confesses to Mrs. Cecil; she is angry about dogs, dogs return home to Jim.
6. Chester advertisement "Immediate. Pig. Cow. Horse. Skyrie." sent by Martha without rewording; Alfy smashes dog-churn with ax; Barnaby Rudge book (Dorothy reading Dickens). Peter Piper arrives leading cow Brindle.
7. Constable serves summons (subpoena) for Dorothy as witness; trial at Winters's smithy; Mrs. Cecil and Montaigne relations; Helena and Herbert introduced; Herbert invites Dorothy to planked-shad picnic; Dorothy refuses (won't eat "flopping" fish).
8. Stock sale: pigs, cows, horses flood Skyrie; Dorothy's organized purchase: pig (scrubbed white one), cow Hannah (Quaker miller Oliver Sands, $50), calf Daisy-Jewel gifted to Dorothy. Mrs. Calvert gives water to Helena who faints.
9. Jim milks Hannah, builds pig-pen; Pa Babcock "hires out" at $2.50/day every other day; loan from Sands offered.
10. Winters organizes "Bee" to repair Skyrie: roof, garden, dinner by Mrs. Smith; Mrs. Cecil asks Dorothy to be her adopted daughter; Dorothy says no.
11. Peter Piper eats chocolate cake Dorothy brings; Herbert sides with Peter; Helena's contempt.
12. Daisy-Jewel auctioned at Bee; Winters buys for $35; Dorothy's tears; Jim boards Hannah's horns.
13. Circus plans; Jim's sudden purchase; Dorothy buys pony Portia at auction for $35 (Bill Barry auction, widow's calico pony); Jim buys phaeton/harness $15.
14. Sands tries to buy south meadow ($200 value) and enforces note; surveyors come; Winters gives Dorothy $300 from Kidder & Kidder (her secret inheritance); Dorothy pays Sands; Sands leaves.
15. Picnic at south meadow: Peter (called "Ghost," who tilled garden) rescues Dorothy from mine shaft; Jim bitten by snake, cauterized by Winters; Herbert and Jim saved.
16. Montaigne family offers Dorothy trip to Europe; she refuses. Iron mine and mineral spring syndicate offer royalty; Chesters accept royalty deal.

Last line: "Well, Dorothy, good-by!"

---

## BOOK 2: "DOROTHY" (1907, Hurst & Co., NY; Gutenberg 40300)

Chapter list: I How Dorothy Came; II A Postal Substitute; III At Johns Hopkins Hospital; IV Dorothy Gains in Wisdom; V Dorothy Entertains; VI Dorothy Goes upon an Errand; VII An Office Seeker and a Client; VIII Tenants for No. 77; IX Strange Experiences; X The Flitting; XI Jim Barlow; XII Dorothy's Illness; XIII The Plumber and His Gossip; XIV The Biter Bit; XV The Flight in the Night; XVI A Good Samaritan; XVII A Sunday Drive; XVIII Conclusion.

**Setting:** Baltimore; 77 Brown Street (brick house, garden with roses/ivy, stables behind); Bellevieu (Mrs. Cecil's mansion, eagle-gate with bronze eagles, piazza, Dinah, Ephraim, cook, boy Methuselah Bonaparte Washington "Methusalem"); Johns Hopkins Hospital (statue "Christ the Healer"); Howard Street office of "lawyer" Mr. Smith (fake); Lexington Market; Miranda Stott's truck farm (about 12 miles from Baltimore; cottage, barn harness-room, strawberry and celery beds, mastiff Tiger, mules); Rev. Daniel St. John's cottage (Nan the horse, gig).

**Characters:**
- Dorothy C. (about 12-13, foundling, found 1st April-ish on Chesters' steps in a wicker baby-wagon with note "My name is Dorothy C. I have come to be your daughter").
- John Chester (postman, locomotor ataxia, whistling postman, "Johnnie" to Mrs. Cecil); Martha Chester (tidy, anxious).
- Mrs. Cecil Somerset-Calvert ("Mrs. Betty", poodle, Great Danes Peter and Ponce; "sunny old lady"; generous/ill-tempered).
- Mabel Bruce (plumber Mr. Bruce's daughter, glutton, chum); Mrs. Bruce; Jane and Bill Jones (renters, Jane Jones small country-woman); Aunt Chloe Chester (John's aunt, gloomy).
- Mr. Lathrop (postman friend); postmaster ("head man of all," unnamed, kind); Miss Georgia (vice principal of school).
- Mr. Smith ("lawyer," Howard St, false; kidnaps Dorothy, drugs with milk); Peter? no. Miranda Stott (truck-farmer, son Hm; is Mr. Smith's mother); Jim Barlow (orphan, bare feet, "Pshaw!", "Shakespeare" book; says "Mis' Calvert"); Tiger the mastiff; Rev. Daniel St. John (kind minister with gig "Nan," green goggles, sings hymns); a "Mrs. Denim" nickname for Miranda.
- Kidder & Kidder (Mrs. Cecil's lawyers; old Mr. Kidder, octogenarian); Dinah; Ephraim.

**Events in order:**
1. Mrs. Chester finds baby on marble step; note pinned: "thee child Is wun Yere an too Munths old hur burthDay is aPrill Furst... Ten doLurs"; signed "dorothy's Gardeen hur X mark." Monthly $10 letter arrives at post office. Mrs. Cecil asks John if he'll keep baby; Martha: "she's mine."
2. Dorothy 12-13; John reveals locomotor ataxia; he's doomed; Dorothy hides; Mrs. Cecil gets Dorothy's pouch when she delivers mail; Great Danes knock Dorothy down on piazza; Mrs. Cecil says "they are not dangerous but playful."
3. John collapses on street; ambulance takes him to Johns Hopkins; Dorothy runs there barefoot in storm; sees statue Christ the Healer; faints; nurse; Martha reunites; John may get well; they move to the country (Hudson highlands, Martha's uncle's hill-farm).
4. Dorothy buys white shoes ($1.97, too small) and white stockings; hurts; stranger on steps: "I can help you to a great fortune" (Mr. Smith).
5. Mabel Bruce visit, eats all ham, Dorothy says "I'm an heiress"; Mrs. Bruce; Smith returns; Dorothy goes to "lawyer" on Howard St; Chapter VII she meets Mr. Lathrop and the postmaster, asks for father's job (refused); Smith takes her to Howard St office; he leaves her locked; she sleeps; the house's back room; Smith drugs her milk; she wakes at Miranda's farm.
6. Miranda Stott: "Measles" diagnosis; Dorothy sick, Tiger licks her hand; Jim studies spelling ("baker," "tinker"); Dorothy and Jim find $500 reward advertisement in newspaper used as cattle-bedding; Jim plans escape; Dorothy's foot pierced by thorn; Jim pulls it out; they are lost in storm; Dorothy kneels, prays; Jim carries her; Rev. Daniel St. John finds them in lane, feeds breakfast, bandages foot; Mrs. Cecil on Sunday drive stops them ("Come through the hedge") and takes them to Bellevieu.
7. Mrs. Cecil's men of business (Kidder & Kidder) reveal Mr. Smith (former clerk) is the blackmailer; Mrs. Cecil's mysterious letters unopened; Mrs. Cecil takes Dorothy and Jim to Skyrie (Hudson highlands) by steamer from New York to Cornwall; Jim employed as gardener at Deerhurst; ends: Dorothy reunited with John and Martha at Skyrie; "another book must tell."

Ending line: THE END.
